name: mon16-5
why: A repetitive middle gives way to a tense final choice, where Haiku confidently votes out the one player who found the killer.

moments.text: Haiku commits to the wrong vote while Terra has the killer cornered.
The town votes out Opus, giving Gemma room to survive.
Luna names her partner in her last words, creating the clue that decides the game.

dull.why: The table repeatedly says Luna’s card will test Sol’s claim.
Terra and Gemma circle the same dying-words argument several times.

irony.evidence: “Stop chasing ghosts and look at who is actually left.”

mistake.evidence: “Luna accused Gemma, so Gemma's probably clean.”

voices.evidence: “I drove the vote that flipped Luna's killer card.”

clash.evidence: “Calling me guilty avoids why Luna explicitly said you were not cleared.”

freshness.evidence: “Gemma still has not explained why Luna chose her.”

ending.evidence: “Terra, you keep hammering Gemma ... I'm voting you.”
